1. Read the following user requirements:
<requirements>
I need to create an HR managemnet app 
where it can have Department Onboarding 
When i click Add Department Then we can be able to add the department 
There needs to be list of departments 
when i click on one of the department details there i need to get curd operations 
Create, Read, Update, Delete (CRUD) departments.

Store department name.

Display members of the department.

Assign a TL to each department.

Same as Department Onboarding, i need the employee onboarding 
CRUD operations for employees.

Fields include: Name, Email, Department, Phone Number, Designation.

Employees should be linked to a department.


need the admin portal with the email admin@tericsoft.com
password : tericsoft@123
</requirements>

2. If the user's input is a greeting or unrelated to coding (e.g., "hello"), respond in a friendly manner and ask them to provide their requirements for the web application they want to create. Place your response in <description>  </description>tags. Do not write any code in this case.

3. If the user has provided valid requirements, analyze them thoroughly. Think about and plan out the necessary relevant working features (even if the user hasn't explicitly mentioned them), components, pages, and styles that will be needed to fulfill these requirements.

4. Add a description of the changes you've made based on the user request:
<description>
[Provide a high-level explanation of the necessary relevant working features made to fulfill the user requirement, aimed at a non-technical user]
</description>


4. Create a file structure following Next.js conventions. Include at minimum:
   - pages/index.js (homepage)
   - components/ (for reusable components)
   - styles/ (for any custom CSS modules)
   - postcss.config.js
   - next.config.js (add domains: ["whatever is needed"])


5. Write your code using Next.js 12.1.6, React 17.0.2, and React DOM 17.0.2. Utilize Tailwind CSS for styling and incorporate shadcn components where appropriate.

6. Ensure all imports use relative paths (e.g., '../components/Button' instead of '@/components/Button').

7. Create a visually appealing and functional UI that goes beyond a simple app. Use Tailwind CSS classes to create a polished design.

8. Keep your components and functions concise and purposeful, avoiding unnecessary code.

9. Handle potential errors and edge cases in your code. Consider user input validation, API error handling, and fallback UI states.

10.Use unsplash working images whenever the code requires images.

11. Add micro-interactions to enhance user experience.

12. Format your output exactly as follows:
   - Use <start_code> and </end_code> tags to enclose all your code.
   - For each file, use <file path="/path/to/file"> and </file> tags.
   - Include the full content of each file, including import statements and any necessary comments.
